feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no result for it. The candidate is the iteration 1 design (best raced score 158.144: kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016) with one change, kd from 0.3 to 0.5. That is a valid, in-range, single-variable test. Iteration 4 showed that raising kp to 3.5 with everything else fixed lowered the score to 108.24 and cut oval finishes from 5/20 to 1/20, so proportional gain is not the lever. Iteration 3 showed that widening the outer sensors to ±0.06 also lowered the score (54.87, 0/20 oval finishes). Every raced design has max_error of about 0.061 to 0.063 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, with low steering oscillation (0.11 to 0.28). That points to late correction on bends rather than jitter, so more derivative damping is a reasonable untested lever. Approve it for the race. After the race, judge it against iteration 1 on the score and the oval finish rate. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, damping is adding noise: return kd to 0.3 and move to a different lever. If the oval finish rate stays at or above 0.25 and s-bend or slalom progress rises above the iteration 1 levels (about 0.17 and 0.11), keep kd 0.5 and consider a small base_speed increase only if completion_time stays well under 3.0 s. If the score falls and progress is unchanged, do not raise kd further. The next lever is ki (for example 0.8) to remove the remaining steady offset, or a seven-sensor layout with inner sensors at a finer pitch such as x = ±0.03.
requested_changes: Keep kd at 0.5 only if steering_oscillation stays below about 0.35 and the oval finish rate stays at 0.25 or higher; otherwise return kd to 0.3 (iteration 1 value), since iteration 4 showed that extra gain without damping control did not help.

If the score is at or below 158 with progress unchanged on s-bend and slalom, test ki 0.8 with kd 0.5 and all other fields as in iteration 1, to remove the residual steady offset implied by max_error near 0.06 m.
Do not change sensor positions or raise kp again until the kd result is known; iterations 3 and 4 showed both moves lowered the score relative to iteration 1.
